questions.question: Trace the complete flow from writing Hello.java to it printing output. Name all six hand-offs and who performs each.
Which hand-offs are compile-time and which are run-time? Put a compile error and a NoClassDefFoundError on the right steps.
Why does javac emit bytecode instead of machine code? What does that buy, and where does native code eventually come from?
What's inside a .class file (magic number, constant pool, method bytecode) and how does the JVM use each part downstream?
The JVM is a stack machine. Given `static int add(int a,int b){return a+b;}`, predict the bytecode and explain each opcode.
How does `java Hello` start execution? What is the initial class, and when does the JVM terminate?
Why can Kotlin/Scala run on the JVM? At which hand-off do they join, and what does that imply about the language vs the platform?
